question.text: Negative basis in commodity futures indicates:

answer.text: A contango market where futures price exceeds spot price
A backwardation market where spot exceeds futures
The commodity cannot be delivered physically

explanation.text: The Logic: Basis = Spot price - Futures price. A negative basis means the spot price is lower than the futures price, so the futures price exceeds the spot price; this configuration is described as a contango market. The Trap: A positive basis (spot above futures) corresponds to backwardation, not contango. Negative basis alone does not imply an arbitrage-free market, and the ability to deliver physically is a separate market-microstructure question unrelated to the sign of the basis. Note: Contango typically reflects the cost of carrying the commodity (storage, financing, insurance) until delivery, while backwardation tends to be associated with tight near-term supply or strong immediate demand.
